Application Materials.content:
As part of your application, you must provide the following supporting documents:
- **Your official transcript.** Please read UCL's guide on [getting your academic transcript](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/getting-your-academic-transcript "Getting your academic transcript").
- **A personal statement.** UCL's [personal statement guidance](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/writing-your-personal-statement "Writing your personal statement") offers advice on writing an effective personal statement.
- If you need a visa to study at UCL you will need to provide a copy of your current **passport**. If you do not have a valid passport, you can complete UCL's Missing passport document and provide your passport later.
- Some courses require additional documents as part of the application; full details are on UCL's [additional course requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/degree-types/courses-additional-requirements "Courses with additional requirements") page.
- If you meet UCL's [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/english-language-requirements "English Language requirements") using a UCL-recognised test, you should upload your official test report form or qualification.
The number of references needed to support your application can be found on the prospectus page for your course. You should contact your nominated referee(s) before starting your application to check they can provide a reference for you.
Do not password-protect or encrypt files. Before submitting, make sure you have uploaded the correct version of each supporting document and that your official transcripts clearly show your name, your institution, and a list of your modules and any grades you have received. You cannot replace or add additional documents once you have submitted your application. You should also provide accurate details of any work experience or previous employment you would like UCL to be aware of, either in the employment section or as part of your uploaded CV, and upload any compulsory supporting documents required for your course to proceed.

Application Deadlines.content:
Programme starts **September 2026**.
Applications accepted:
- Applicants who require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 26 Jun 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.
- Applicants who do not require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **An upper second-class UK Bachelor's degree** in a health, science, business or economics related subject or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard.
- Graduates without the relevant degree classification but with extensive relevant work experience are welcome to apply and will be considered on an individual basis.
- For application to the analytics specialism, UCL additionally encourages an interest and aptitude in engaging with quantitative data to support healthcare management.
- China-specific equivalent qualifications: a **four-year bachelor’s degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered. For the **upper second-class (2:1)** requirement, applicants from UCL’s list of Chinese universities need a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 85%**; applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%**. UCL’s list includes a selection of Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities, but not all universities from these projects are included.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language level for this course is: **Level 1**.
[UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses) are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL. Further information can be found on UCL's [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/learning-and-living-ucl/international-students/english-language-requirements) page.
- **IELTS Academic Version:** **Overall score of 6.5 and a minimum of 6.0 in each component**. Applicants may take the IELTS Academic Online test. UCL does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake.
- **TOEFL, tests taken from 21 January 2026:** **Overall score of 4.5 and 4.0 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**.
- **TOEFL, tests taken before 21 January 2026:** **Overall score of 92 with 24/30 in reading and writing and 20/30 in speaking and listening**. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL's institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- **Cambridge English: C2 Proficiency (CPE):** **Overall score of 176 with 169 in all subtests**.
- **Cambridge English: C1 Advanced (CAE):** **Overall score of 176 with 169 in all subtests**.
- **Pearson Test of English (Academic):** **Overall score of 75 with a minimum of 67 in each Communicative Skill**.

Program Overview.content:
Global Healthcare Management (Analytics) MSc is taught in London, Stratford at UCL East. Study modes are full-time, part-time, and flexible, with durations of 1 calendar year, 2 calendar years, and 5 calendar years respectively.
A course with tangible real-world value, the Global Healthcare Management (Analytics) MSc is a degree that has been co-created by academics and industry experts. It equips students with essential skills and connections to change the world in healthcare through opportunities to specialise in analytics.
Taught at the world’s first business school dedicated to health in a global top 10 university (QS World University Rankings 2026), this course offers an opportunity to learn from the sector while gaining valuable and in-demand skills. Equipping students with a critical foundation in the theories, principles and practices underpinning healthcare management, the Global Healthcare Management MSc empowers future healthcare managers and leaders with knowledge. Learning about global differences and interconnections, quality improvement, patient safety and workforce management are also fundamentals on this course. A group business project ensures that problem-solving and innovation in the healthcare context are qualities instilled in all students.
This course is taught from UCL’s state-of-the-art bespoke facilities on the [UCL East campus](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/ucl-east/), on the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in east London. The UCL Global Business School for Health is situated in the Marshgate building with access to hi-tech teaching areas and collaboration spaces, a library, and a refectory.
The course is ideal for individuals who strive to become excellent managers and changemakers within healthcare settings. Applicants may be new or recent graduates in a health, science or business field, or have relevant work experience in healthcare. For the analytics specialism, UCL additionally encourages an interest and aptitude in engaging with quantitative data to support healthcare management.
Graduates of the Global Healthcare Management MSc with a specialist route in analytics can expect to gain a wide-ranging understanding of healthcare management; skills in data analytics to support healthcare management; the ability to analyse statistical data, technological and information sources to support healthcare management decisions; significant research and analytical skills for data-driven healthcare management; communication skills for healthcare managers and leaders; expertise to assess value for patients, organisations and society; the ability to manage and lead a diverse workforce; and experience in teamwork, collaboration, innovation and continuous professional development.
Graduates are likely to pursue careers with private, non-profit and multinational organisations in the policy or analytics space. Recent graduate destinations include PhD study, including securing scholarship opportunities, and data analytics at AstraZeneca. Paths after the course include public, private or non-governmental organisations in health and healthcare, healthcare specialisms in professional services, and government and public bodies.
Teaching is primarily through face-to-face lectures and seminars/tutorials across Terms 1 and 2, with weekly group seminars, case-based presentations and discussions, and project development workshops. In Term 3, students undertake a business project with colleagues, drawing on interaction with an industry mentor and project supervisor, and complete an individual desk-based research project under the mentorship of a research supervisor. Assessment includes written exams, coursework essays, presentations, a business project, a research project, and health and business case written analysis.
The analytics route develops breadth and depth of understanding of global healthcare management challenges and opportunities in the digital age. Students gain an advanced understanding of the role of data applied to business and management for healthcare and focus on applying these tools within the global health landscape. All students complete two projects: a group business project developing an idea for a healthcare improvement from concept to business case report and presentation, and a research project critically examining an aspect or question related to analytics learning. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits; upon successful completion of 180 credits, they are awarded an MSc in Global Healthcare Management (Analytics).

Curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time, Part-time, Flexible. Duration: 1 calendar year, 2 calendar years, 5 calendar years. The course is taught at UCL East in London, Stratford.
Module teaching is primarily in the form of face-to-face lectures and seminars/tutorials across Terms 1 and 2. In Term 3, students embark on the business project and finish the individual desk-based research project. Full-time students can expect 15 to 18 hours per week in Terms 1 and 2 in face-to-face teaching sessions, plus 17 to 20 hours per week in self-directed study. Part-time and flexible students study at a pro-rata rate.
Full-time: The Global Healthcare Management MSc course with an analytics route offers breadth and depth of understanding of global healthcare management challenges and opportunities in this digital age. On the analytics route, students gain an advanced understanding of the role of data applied to business and management for healthcare and focus on the application of these tools within the global health landscape, as well as further develop analytic skills.
All students complete two projects:
- A group business project involving developing an idea for a healthcare improvement from concept to business case report and presentation.
- A research project where students work on a research paper that critically examines an aspect or question related to the selected route, analytics.
Part-time: The two-year part-time structure consists of 180 credits. Students take 90 credits in Year 1 and Year 2.
Flexible: The modular/flexible structure gives students the flexibility to take 180 credits worth of modules over three-five years. Students can choose as many or as few modules as they wish each year.
Compulsory modules:
- [Economic Evaluation and Health Financing](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/economic-evaluation-and-health-financing-GBSH0011)
- [Organisational Behaviour for an Inclusive and Diverse Workforce](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/organisational-behaviour-for-an-inclusive-and-diverse-workforce-GBSH0012)
- [Leadership and Management in Global Healthcare](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/leadership-and-management-in-global-healthcare-GBSH0010)
- [Principles of Health Data Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/principles-of-health-data-analytics-CHME0001)
- [Principles of Health Data Science](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/principles-of-health-data-science-CHME0012)
- [Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare (AIH)](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/artificial-intelligence-in-healthcare-aih-CHME0016)
- [Changing Health Systems](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/changing-health-systems-GBSH0007)
- [Business Project](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/business-project-GBSH0008)
- [Research Project](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/research-project-GBSH0009)
Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, students will be awarded an MSc in Global Healthcare Management (Analytics).

- Undergraduate or Postgraduate student in shared privately-rented accommodation: shared house rent range, excluding household bills, **£150-300 per week**, **£650-1300 per month**, **£7,800-15,600 per 52 week contract**.

Financial Aid.content:
- Global Healthcare Leaders scholarship: for students who show exceptional leadership potential in their fields and want to make a difference in healthcare.
- Value: £10,000 or £15,000. Selection criteria: based on academic merit. Eligibility: UK, Overseas. Level: Postgraduate taught.
- Applicants must demonstrate academic excellence and exceptional leadership potential, and must have applied to study Global Healthcare Management (Analytics) MSc starting in September 2026.
- To apply, candidates must submit a 500-word essay demonstrating how they will make a difference in healthcare. [Apply now](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=_oivH5ipW0yTySEKEdmlwjGHG6maV4JKsrlDx33IpKZUN1JBWDBJUVo3RFlMS0wzTDRBOVpZTTU3Qy4u)
- Round 1 application deadline: **18 January 2026**; notification date: **16 February 2026**. Round 2 application deadline: **31 March 2026**; notification date: **28 April 2026**. Round 3 application deadline: **26 June 2026**; notification date: **24 July 2026**.
- Candidates can apply for more than one scholarship but if successful, only one scholarship will be awarded. Candidates must submit an application form for each scholarship they wish to apply for.
- £10,000 is awarded to successful candidates with UK fee status. £15,000 is awarded to successful candidates with Overseas fee status.
- If successful in the scholarship application, candidates must accept their offer to study and pay their deposit by the required deadline. Failure to do so may result in the scholarship being withdrawn.
- Scholarships are awarded for the specified intake year only and **cannot be deferred** to a future intake. If a candidate withdraws from the programme before completion, they may be required to **repay the scholarship amount** received.

Multiple Applications.content: Please note - you can only apply to a **maximum of two taught graduate courses in any academic cycle**.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer, except in limited exceptional circumstances. Deferral requests will be considered only for: serious illness of the offer holder or serious illness/death of a parent, guardian, partner or child; parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months; being directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster; being awarded a UCL scholarship or a full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year; or holding an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
- To be eligible for a deferral, you must hold an **unconditional offer which you have accepted**. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme.
- Deferral requests must be made on the offer page of the application portal. Requests due to illness or parental/adoption leave require a letter from a relevant medical practitioner; scholarship-based requests require an official scholarship award letter. UCL may request more information before making a final decision.
- **An application cannot be deferred twice.** Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
- The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
- If a deferral request is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment. A new offer letter will be issued, and a new English test may be required if the current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.
- If the deferral request is unsuccessful, or if you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the listed categories, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but the application will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- You must meet all your conditions and hold an unconditional offer before you can enrol. Your offer letter will contain information on any deadlines that apply to your offer.
- Your offer letter will outline exactly which degree documents you need to provide. UCL cannot accept anything other than final official documents to meet the conditions of your offer.
- If you need to take an English language test to meet your offer conditions, you must provide your official results. UCL will not accept screenshots of your results portal.
- You can take a [UCL Pre-sessional English course](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses/pre-sessional-english-courses/pg) to settle the English language condition in your offer.
- You should still upload your documents, even if you do not meet your academic offer condition. The Admissions team will still consider whether your offer can be confirmed.
- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the UCL level 1 requirement, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer and cannot consider test scores that do not meet the UCL level 1 requirement.
